doc.title: Nick Brignola interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 28, 1997

title: Love/hate relationship with the baritone
summary: He calls himself an alto player at heart, describes fighting the heavy baritone and extending its high range.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Yeah, the older I get it gets a little heavier. Finally get somebody to make a fiberglass one, you know, that comes apart and fits in a box about this big. But anyway it’s been that kind of a thing. But I got to the point where okay, if I’m going to play this thing then I’m going to really play it. And I always attacked it that way. And I always say “attacked” because it’s a big fight. Every time I pick it up it’s a fight. Whereas the alto — I think I’m just an alto player really. I hear the alto better, I feel—
Well your fluency on it sounds like you’re thinking alto almost.

And I always play the high end if you will notice. That’s another reason I tried to extend the range of the baritone to give me more high end. Also no other horn has the range that horn has if you do extend the high range. So I feel I’ve contributed something to the advancement of the horn but more than that it’s just I really enjoy playing it. And when I’m in my top shape I fear no one. But I’d still rather be an alto player.
I think the die’s been cast, actually.
